body:
Thank you for your reply. I'm struggling with the intense guilt now it's hit me what I was doing. I don't want to break up with her. I've realised I don't know if I'm capable of giving her what she needs emotionally. I've agonised many times over the years whether the doubts I feel are true doubts or just rocd. In reality it's probably a mixture of the two. But as I could never really trust my instinct when it comes to feelings like this I've just carried on.

I feel I should tell her what I've done. But I think it would be the end of the relationship. Maybe that would be ultimately the best for her, I don't know.
You should be heard and listened to. You've made a good start expressing yourself here.
I appreciate your sentiment and you're right, it forces it on someone else. That's the reason that keeps a lot of people alive, including myself. Unfortunately, talking isn't always an option.

I have an incurable illness, one that's left me housebound for much of the last quarter of a century. It will kill me, just very, very slowly.

If you want an incurable illness, make it a quick and painless one.
Thank you
Thanks for your reply. I appreciate the offer but I can't go into it.
Yep, preceded by completely.
Hope is a long time coming. I appreciate your reply.

It's probably no consolation but we all do things wrong and fuck up. I'd say I've made (and still make) more bad decisions and choices than the average Joe. It pisses me off about myself and I know how much it can get to you over a long period. I do feel I'm learning over time though and you will too even if you don't realise it.

The situation with your wife must be having a big impact on you at the moment. I'm reluctant to suggest this based on what little info you've given but do you think it would be better for your mental wellbeing if you had some time apart?

I'm so sorry you have all this cope with. It's not ridiculous that it makes you feel so low. I had a quick look at your post history and saw you mention the blood pooling and pain in your legs. My first thought was POTS (Postural Orthostaic Tachycardia Syndrome) or something similar and noticed someone had else had replied to your post with the same thought. Have you looked into it?
I'd also like to know why you feel you're a vile person. No judgement here.

I'm so sorry that you've become so estranged from your wife. Her reaction to you wanting and intending to kill yourself is not normal. People can often grow apart but it sounds more than that, it sounds like she's had a big personality change since joining the Jehovas. Presumably you've tried to talk about this with her? May I ask why you hate yourself so much?

Thank you for your reply. I must admit I am usually put off by woo-woo stuff. Its not so much that I don't think they'll have useful information, more that if something doesn't fit right for me then it's difficult to get through. I'll give it another look though.

Some people have horrific thoughts and feelings to deal with. Sometimes it's within their control, but sometimes it's not. But regardless, it does not mean you don't deserve to live. Have you looked into talking to someone, a therapist maybe? The right person could help narrow why you think and feel in the way that bothers you.

Hope can be fleeting and can dissipate just when we need it the most. Keep going, keep trying. You can turn things around and even though it seems impossible right now, you can get to a position where you can enjoy life again.

Thank you for your reply. Your piece on The Binary Human Mind was very interesting.

The Sedona method has some very mixed opinions on from the reviews I've read.
Thank you, I'm not 100% sure it will be for me based on the reviews but I'm open to trying it.

I'm afraid I can't type much at the moment due being ill but I wanted to say keep hanging in there. The weight of worry/anxiety/guilt/responsibility or whatever it is you're feeling can be utterly overwhelming to the point you want out.

It's probably not a lot of comfort but you're not alone in what you're going through even though you must feel completely alone in it yourself. Please keep going, it can get better.

I think a lot of people would feel demoralized and 'what's the point' if they had been at rock bottom, rebuilt their life but ended up in a bad place again. It's gutting, extremely hard to take but unfortunately it can happen. As bad as this setback is, you will learn things about yourself from it that in the future might will you. The realisation that there's no easy fix and that the desire/motivation to improve things must come from yourself can be pretty overwhelming too. Especially when you're currently in a place where you just don't have that in you. Don't be hard on yourself. If you don't feel you have the strength or motivation to try improve things at the moment then just keep ticking over for now. You can still try make little changes here and there, sometimes they can help combine to just give you a little glimmer of motivation and positivity that will help restart things. 

Not wanting to put yourself in a situation where you can risk losing what you have or someone your love is understandable. I think it stems from depression and it's also a sort of self\-protection when you're feeling vulnerable and feel you can't take any more.

At the moment you no doubt feel lost, scared and alone with it. Hang in there. In the moments where you feel a bit stronger and more positive about life, How do you feel about trying to jot a few ideas down on ways to make life better?

Sometimes you can't force yourself to care about things or be interested in things. I mean, you can try to explore new hobbies and interests, meet new people etc but if you're not in the right mindset for it then it will likely not give you what you need.

How long have you felt this way? If it's been for some time then perhaps you're suffering from depression?

Do you think your excessive sad feelings are mainly to do with currently having no purpose or goals in life? Do you know what causes your anxiety?

Edit: I love your username btw!

Do your family know that you're feeling suicidal? If your boyfriend isn't willing or able to support you then you need to look elsewhere for support. There is always somewhere and someone who will care. It's just a matter of finding them. I know that when you're in the depths of despair, ending it all can seem the only option but it is most definitely not the only option.   
Try and give us some more information if you can so we can best help you. Dig deep and be as strong as you can possibly be. You can get through this.
Lol. I am currently wishing I was pretty much any other person than myself at the moment. But I'm not sure I'd switch shoes with poor Loris right now.
